applies_to: Taco duplex and multiplex domestic water booster pump sets controlled by Danfoss drives (2019 IOM).
summary: Taco booster pump sets run each pump on a Danfoss drive that holds the discharge pressure setpoint. The IOM lists ten important BACnet points on the drive: run/stop and fault reset commands, setpoint 1, the analog input and PID feedback, run, fault and hand/auto status, a running flag and the active set-up. For the full object list it refers to the Danfoss BACnet instructions.
notes: This is the short 'Important BACnet Points for Boosters' list from the IOM, not the drive's full object list.
The IOM writes the last object as MSO:1 'Multi_state_value: 1'; it is listed here as a Multi-state Value.
The BAS wires to drive terminals 68/69 (the Danfoss RS-485 bus), on the lead drive (VFD #1) or daisy-chained through all drives; terminals are not chained at the factory.
Units are not printed; the setpoint and feedback follow the drive's pressure scaling.

source.title: Taco Booster Pump Sets - Installation, Operation, and Maintenance Manual

integration.summary: Set up BACnet on the Danfoss drive per the Danfoss instructions, then use BV 1 to run or stop the booster and AV 30 to set the pressure setpoint. Monitor BV 33 running, BV 5 OK/fault and AV 4 feedback, and reset faults with BV 3.
integration.enable: BV 1 Run/Stop Command starts and stops the booster over BACnet.
setup: BACnet communication is set up in the Danfoss drive; the IOM points to the Danfoss BACnet instructions for details.
Bus terminals are 68 and 69 on each drive; connect the BAS to the lead drive (VFD #1) or daisy-chain all drives as the project needs.
gotchas: Only these ten points are documented by Taco; other drive objects follow the Danfoss object list.
